Article Submission Abstract
This article examines the loan translation strategy of English terminology in Kiswahili and its effects by focusing on the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry through selected entries from the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary (2012). The main aim of this investigation is to assess the contribution of the loan translation of English vocabulary to the overall development of the Kiswahili language. According to this article, this area has not been prioritized among the various translation topics that have already been studied. This has motivated the researcher to address this area. The data for this article was collected in the field from departments and institutions located in the city of Dar es Salaam through interviews, questionnaires, and library-based data sources. The departments and institutions involved in data collection are: the Department of Foreign Languages and Linguistics, TATAKI from the University of Dar es Salaam, as well as BAKIZA. These departments and institutions are located in Ubungo District, Dar es Salaam Region, where the researcher was able to conduct inquiries and hold face-to-face interviews with translation experts. In addition, data was collected from various texts from the library data source. For instance, dictionaries, dissertations, journals, and several books were used, depending on the subject of this article. The objectives of the article have been achieved by being guided by the Theory of Scientific Terminology pioneered by Kiingi (1989) and further developed by Kiingi (1992) and Kiingi (1998), as well as Mwaro-Were (2000, 2001). Likewise, the data for this article was analyzed using a descriptive approach. In addition, the findings have shown that Kiswahili has acquired numerous terminologies in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry through the loan translation strategy. This article is important for linguists as it identifies various English-language terminologies in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry that have been incorporated into Kiswahili through loan translation. Introduction  
Translation is the act of transferring a message contained in writing from the source language to the target language without altering the intended meaning in the source language. Thus, translation is regarded as a method of learning foreign languages, showcasing various cultures, and transmitting the knowledge and skills of other communities, such as information on scientific and technological advancements. The motivation that drives a person to translate the message from the source language to the target language is the desire to facilitate communication among speakers of different languages. We can therefore say that translation is a means or even a bridge to bring together various communities that speak different languages. Moreover, loan translation is one method of coining new vocabulary, where a concept from the source language is adopted and translated into the target language; for example, Army worm – kiwavi jeshi, tap root – mzizi pau, and so on. The strategy of borrowing through loan translation has gained momentum due to the significant developments occurring in the field of science and technology, coupled with society’s advancement into modernity, resulting in a high demand for vocabulary to describe various concepts. The researcher of this article investigates the loan translation strategy of English vocabulary into Kiswahili. The researcher has focused on the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry through selected entries from the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary (2012). The main objective is to evaluate the contribution of loan translation of English vocabulary to the overall development of the Kiswahili language. Translation work has been carried out numerous times around the world (Mwansoko, 1996; Malangwa, 2005; Giambruno, 2008; Baker & Saldanha, 2008; Malangwa, 2010; Malangwa, 2014). Crystal (2002) explains that new technology often has an impact on language, whether written or spoken. This is the reason why the English language has influenced Swahili at the lexical level. Furthermore, Crystal (2004) observes that the greatest influence on the lexical development of Swahili has come from English, which is the main language of Information and Communication Technology, as well as from Arabic. Mwaro-Were (2000), along with Adika and Kevogo (2014), explain that since ancient times, lexical borrowing has had a significant influence on the Swahili language. Lexicologically, several foreign languages have influenced Swahili to varying degrees. Some of these languages are Portuguese, Persian, Arabic, Hindi, German, and English. This clearly demonstrates that advancements in science and technology have had a significant impact on the Swahili language. Translation plays a role in promoting and spreading a language, especially through the process of transferring structural expressions from the source language to the target language. Additionally, translation brings satisfaction to the translator when they successfully complete their work effectively (Mwansoko, 2016). Nassor (2017), for his part, explains that the rate of coining Swahili terminology has increased significantly in recent years compared to the 1960s. He further adds that at the end of the 19th century, the Swahili community experienced major advancements in science and technology, as well as in other fields. As a result, the Swahili language has undergone significant changes. Therefore, efforts to develop Swahili terminologically intensified in order to keep pace with these advancements. Alongside studies that examine the development of the Swahili language due to advancements in science and technology, this article also addresses this issue but focuses specifically on the field of loan translation in the areas of biology, physics, and chemistry. Adolph (2019), on his part, investigated terminology in the fields of medicine and computers, originating from English in Swahili and the processes of their adaptation. His research findings clearly demonstrate that Swahili has expanded its vocabulary through the adaptation of medical and computer-related terms from English. Consequently, this adaptation has contributed to the growth of Swahili due to the significant expansion of scientific and technological vocabulary in the areas of computers and medicine. Language grows and changes every day according to the development of society. One of the main criteria for the growth and change of a language is the increase in terminology. According to Adolph (2019), in order for terminologies to increase in a language, new terms must be created. Terms are formed in a language so that its culture can accommodate concepts that were previously not part of that culture. This note is very important in this article as it shows how language grows and meets the communication needs among community members. This article examines the strategy of loan translation of English terminology into Swahili and its effects by focusing on the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry, in contrast to Adolph's (2019) study, which investigates the development of the Swahili language through the adaptation of medical and computer terminology. Many scholars who have addressed borrowing agree that borrowing is the transfer of lexical elements from one language to another (Haugen, 1950; Polomé, 1980; Adolph, 2014; Winford, 2003). This article is divided into five sections: The first section is the introduction, in which the general concept of translation and its functions are explained, together with the concept of loan translation. The second section explains the theory that guided the analysis of the data in this article. The third section describes the methodology. The fourth section analyzes data on the strategy of loan translation from English into Swahili and its effects. The discussion concerns terminology in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry from the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary (2012). The fifth section is the conclusion. Theory  
The Theory of Scientific Terminology was used to provide data for this article. The Theory of Scientific Terminology is associated with Kiingi (1989), who is the original founder of this theory. Later, this theory was further developed by Kiingi (1992, 1998); Mwaro-Were (2000, 2001); Kevogo, Mukuthuria, and Ontieri (2018); and Kevogo (2020). This theory contains scientific criteria for effective terminology, which play a central role in the evaluation conducted in our article. Several scholars, such as Tumbo-Masabo and Mwansoko (2008), have clearly outlined various principles that should be followed during the borrowing, adaptation, and formation of terminology from indigenous and foreign languages into Swahili. These principles are elaborated in Tumbo-Masabo and Mwansoko (2008). This involves creating terminology using Swahili, Bantu languages, other African languages, and foreign languages. In addition to many other views expressed by Tumbo-Masabo and Mwansoko (1997) regarding these principles, they recommend the following guidelines: Terminology should reflect the distinctive features of the concepts they represent (or at least suggest such features) and be clear to the intended users. If terminology is formed using compounding and word combination techniques, the following aspects must be considered:
The number of words combined or joined should not exceed two. Hyphens should not be used to separate compound terms, because in Swahili such terms are usually pronounced as a single word, with the primary stress on only one syllable. For example: -zao mtiririko ("flow products") and -nusu kipenyo ("semi-diameter"). Such terms should not have more than four syllables, since Swahili words usually have an average of between one and five syllables. Terminology must be highly derivable in order to generate other related terms within the relevant domain or field. This will allow terms representing closely related or derivationally connected concepts to logically reflect that connection. For example: taifa ("nation"), taifisha ("nationalize"), utaifa ("nationalism"), -a kitaifa ("national"), -sio na taifa ("stateless"), and -siyo wa taifa ("un-national"). Terminology (especially those with overlapping shades of meaning) must maintain consistency in sequence. The following terms, for example, demonstrate an acceptable alignment of sequence: tabakanje, tabakandani, tabakamzunguko, tabakakati, and so on. Terminology must be adequate, meaning it should reflect the characteristics of the concepts they represent (and not, for instance, contradict them). For example, the term “tahakiki ya maandishi” is inappropriate because it generally refers to the evaluation of writing at large, rather than the analysis or critique of literature. Terminology must also be short and understandable. Lengthy terms, such as “majira ya majani kupukutika” (when the dry season approaches), are unsuitable because they do not adhere to the principle of linguistic economy. These principles are essential in terminology creation as they provide guidance on what should be done regarding borrowing, formation, and adaptation. In addition, methods for creating terminology have been proposed. Let us look at these methods below: first, translation, especially from languages known to be international, such as English, French, Spanish, and so on. Second, forming terminology based on conceptual frameworks. This theory is relevant as it provides the foundations to follow during the translation process. Likewise, it clarifies the methods of terminology creation. 

Methodology  
Every researcher uses appropriate and clear methods for their research. This article is the result of a descriptive research conducted both in the library and in the field. The researcher collected data from the Department of Foreign Languages and Linguistics, TATAKI from the University of Dar es Salaam, as well as BAKIZA in Ubungo District, Dar es Salaam Region, where data was gathered using interviews, questionnaires, and a library data source. According to Krishnaswami and Ranganatham (2005), interviews are a data collection method that involves an exchange between the researcher and the respondent with the aim of obtaining information related to the topic under investigation. Using the interview method, the researcher was able to conduct face-to-face interviews with translation experts from the aforementioned departments and institutions. A questionnaire is prepared with the aim of collecting important information from respondents (Mugenda and Mugenda, 2003). The questionnaire method can be conducted either face-to-face or through non-face-to-face means, depending on advancements in science and technology. Advancements in science and technology have facilitated the sending of various questionnaires by researchers to their respondents electronically (via web and email). However, the researcher of this article used face-to-face questionnaires because the informants were in the same location and easily accessible. In addition, the researcher reviewed various writings such as journals, dissertations, dictionaries, and so on from the library data source. Research Findings

The findings of this article were obtained after an investigation and analysis of data concerning the development of Swahili through the loan translation of terminology from English. Loan translation is a strategy for term creation involving word-for-word transfer of both structural elements and general concepts. The structure of terms created using the loan translation strategy changes to conform to the morphological and phonological rules of the target language. From the methods of interviews, questionnaires, and the library data source, it was found that several terms in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry—through the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary (2012)—have been incorporated into Swahili from English via the loan translation strategy. The findings of this article indicate that terminology in biology, chemistry, and physics has been translated through the strategy of loan translation from English into Swahili. This is due to the high demand for these terms among Swahili users, as well as the development and growth of science and technology. This situation compels Swahili to use the loan translation strategy in order to meet the communication needs of Swahili speakers and to incorporate concepts derived from these terms. Benefits for Language Translators and Global Recognition of TUKI

The strategy of borrowing English terms into Swahili through loan translation as a method for creating Swahili terminology has played a significant role in providing opportunities for language translators. For instance, TUKI (2012) has translated an adequate vocabulary related to the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry by employing the loan translation strategy and other forms of borrowing; however, this article focuses on the loan translation strategy. This institution has translated vocabulary from biology, physics, and chemistry from English into Swahili. Indeed, this work has brought global recognition to TUKI due to its great importance in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry. Alongside international recognition, those involved in this work have also benefited economically from sales made through published books, including the standardized Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary. This is attributed to the significance of its contents, the care taken in its preparation, and especially the expertise and professionalism of the dictionary’s compilers. This clearly demonstrates that its users have great confidence in this dictionary and are therefore willing to make purchases without hesitation. The Global Spread of the Swahili Language

Based on information from respondents (field data) as well as library data, the researcher has found that the loan translation strategy implemented by TUKI (2012) has contributed to the worldwide recognition of Swahili, since the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry are used globally due to advancements in science and technology, as well as their importance to students studying these subjects and to Swahili speakers in general. Furthermore, speakers of other languages apart from Swahili need to learn the vocabulary of these fields in the Swahili language. This situation leads them to acquire several Swahili language books, including this dictionary. All these factors have significantly contributed to the overall spread of Swahili throughout the world. The global spread of Swahili has encouraged people from various countries to learn Swahili, appreciate it, and value it highly.

Conclusion

The analysis in this article confirms the argument that the loan translation strategy has been used as one of the methods for borrowing English terminology into Swahili. The terms examined in this article are those from the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry. In the case of biology, terms such as: abductor, abiotic, aerial roots, basal bone, biennial plants, nitrogen, occiput, spermatid, and zoology were identified. The researcher also considered the loan translation strategy in the field of chemistry. The following are some of the terms addressed in this field: absolute, acetate, active mass, masi tendaji, acylation, bond energy, pesticide, x-radiation, and zymology. Additionally, the researcher of this article has also examined the effects of the loan translation strategy on the Swahili language, language translators, students of biology, physics, and chemistry, speakers of other languages learning Swahili, and Swahili speakers in general. The findings of this article have revealed that this strategy has been beneficial to language translators, especially those translating from English into Swahili. A good example is the experts at TUKI who translated terms from these fields from English into Swahili. These translators have improved economically due to the global sale of this dictionary. It has also become evident that TUKI, which is now known as TATAKI, has become recognized and established worldwide. Makala haya yanachunguza mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo wa istilahi za Kiingereza katika Kiswahili na athari zake kwa kuzingatia fani za biolojia, fizikia na kemia kupitia maingizo teule kutoka katika Kamusi ya Biolojia, Fizikia na Kemia (2012). Kwa mujibu wa makala haya, eneo hili halijapewa kipaumbele miongoni mwa mada mbalimbali za tafsiri ambazo tayari zimesomwa. Hili limemtia motisha mtafiti kushughulikia eneo hili. Idara na taasisi zinazohusika na ukusanyaji wa takwimu ni: Idara ya Lugha za Kigeni na Isimu, TATAKI kutoka Chuo Kikuu cha Dar es Salaam, pamoja na BAKIZA. Idara na taasisi hizo ziko Wilaya ya Ubungo Mkoa wa Dar es Salaam ambapo mtafiti aliweza kufanya uchunguzi na kufanya mahojiano ya ana kwa ana na wataalamu wa tafsiri. Malengo ya makala haya yamefikiwa kwa kuongozwa na Nadharia ya Istilahi za Kisayansi iliyoanzishwa na Kiingi (1989) na kuendelezwa zaidi na Kiingi (1992) na Kiingi (1998), pamoja na Mwaro-Were (2000, 2001). Utangulizi  
Tafsiri ni kitendo cha kuhamisha ujumbe ulio katika maandishi kutoka lugha chanzi hadi lugha lengwa bila kubadilisha maana iliyokusudiwa katika lugha chanzi. Kwa hivyo, tafsiri inachukuliwa kuwa njia ya kujifunza lugha za kigeni, kuonyesha tamaduni mbalimbali, na kusambaza ujuzi na ujuzi wa jamii nyingine, kama vile habari juu ya maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia. Motisha inayomsukuma mtu kutafsiri ujumbe kutoka lugha chanzi hadi lugha lengwa ni hamu ya kurahisisha mawasiliano miongoni mwa wazungumzaji wa lugha mbalimbali. Kwa hiyo tunaweza kusema kuwa tafsiri ni njia au hata daraja la kuzikutanisha jamii mbalimbali zinazozungumza lugha mbalimbali. Aidha, tafsiri ya mkopo ni mbinu mojawapo ya kubuni msamiati mpya, ambapo dhana kutoka katika lugha chanzi hupitishwa na kutafsiriwa katika lugha lengwa; kwa mfano, Army worm – kiwavi jeshi, tap root – mzizi pau, na kadhalika. Mkakati wa kukopa kupitia tafsiri ya mkopo umeshika kasi kutokana na maendeleo makubwa yanayotokea katika nyanja ya sayansi na teknolojia, pamoja na maendeleo ya jamii katika usasa, na kusababisha uhitaji mkubwa wa msamiati wa kuelezea dhana mbalimbali. Mtafiti wa makala haya anachunguza mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo wa msamiati wa Kiingereza hadi Kiswahili. Mtafiti amejikita katika fani za baiolojia, fizikia na kemia kupitia maingizo teule kutoka katika Kamusi ya Biolojia, Fizikia na Kemia (2012). Lengo kuu ni kutathmini mchango wa tafsiri ya mkopo ya msamiati wa Kiingereza katika maendeleo ya jumla ya lugha ya Kiswahili. Kazi ya kutafsiri imefanywa mara nyingi duniani kote (Mwansoko, 1996; Malangwa, 2005; Giambruno, 2008; Baker & Saldanha, 2008; Malangwa, 2010; Malangwa, 2014). Crystal (2002) anaeleza kuwa teknolojia mpya mara nyingi huwa na athari katika lugha, iwe ya maandishi au ya mazungumzo. Hii ndiyo sababu lugha ya Kiingereza imeathiri Kiswahili katika kiwango cha kileksika. Zaidi ya hayo, Crystal (2004) anaona kuwa ushawishi mkubwa zaidi katika ukuzaji wa kileksika wa Kiswahili umetokana na Kiingereza, ambayo ndiyo lugha kuu ya Teknolojia ya Habari na Mawasiliano, na pia kutoka Kiarabu. Mwaro-Were (2000), pamoja na Adika na Kevogo (2014), wanaeleza kuwa tangu zamani, ukopaji wa kileksia umekuwa na athari kubwa katika lugha ya Kiswahili. Kileksikolojia, lugha kadhaa za kigeni zimeathiri Kiswahili kwa viwango tofauti. Baadhi ya lugha hizo ni Kireno, Kiajemi, Kiarabu, Kihindi, Kijerumani, na Kiingereza. Hii inadhihirisha wazi kwamba maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia yamekuwa na athari kubwa katika lugha ya Kiswahili. Tafsiri ina mchango mkubwa katika kukuza na kueneza lugha, hasa kupitia mchakato wa kuhamisha semi za kimuundo kutoka lugha chanzi hadi lugha lengwa. Zaidi ya hayo, tafsiri huleta kuridhika kwa mfasiri anapomaliza kazi yake kwa ufanisi (Mwansoko, 2016). Nassor (2017), kwa upande wake, anaeleza kuwa kasi ya utunzi wa istilahi za Kiswahili imeongezeka sana katika miaka ya hivi karibuni ikilinganishwa na miaka ya 1960. Anaongeza kuwa mwishoni mwa karne ya 19, jamii ya Waswahili ilipata maendeleo makubwa katika sayansi na teknolojia, na pia katika nyanja nyinginezo. Kutokana na hali hiyo, lugha ya Kiswahili imekuwa na mabadiliko makubwa. Kwa hivyo, juhudi za kukikuza Kiswahili kiistilahi ziliongezeka ili kuendana na maendeleo haya. Kando na tafiti zinazochunguza maendeleo ya lugha ya Kiswahili kutokana na maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia, makala haya pia yanaangazia suala hili lakini yanaangazia haswa nyanja ya tafsiri ya mkopo katika nyanja za biolojia, fizikia na kemia. Adolph (2019), kwa upande wake, alichunguza istilahi katika nyanja za utabibu na kompyuta, zikitoka katika Kiingereza cha Kiswahili na taratibu za kuzirekebisha. Matokeo ya utafiti wake yanadhihirisha wazi kuwa Kiswahili kimepanua msamiati wake kupitia utohoaji wa istilahi za kimatibabu na kompyuta kutoka Kiingereza. Hivyo basi, utohozi huu umechangia kukua kwa Kiswahili kutokana na kupanuka kwa msamiati wa kisayansi na kiteknolojia katika nyanja za kompyuta na tiba. Mtaalamu huyu anasema kuwa moja ya athari za utohozi ni kuongezeka kwa istilahi za Kiingereza ndani ya Kiswahili, na hivyo 2 Hapana. Mkakati wa Kutafsiri Istilahi za Kiingereza kwa Kiswahili na Athari Zake: Uchambuzi wa Maingizo Teule kutoka katika Kamusi ya Biolojia, Fizikia na Kemia ili kukidhi mahitaji ya mawasiliano miongoni mwa wanajamii. Lugha hukua na kubadilika kila siku kulingana na maendeleo ya jamii. Moja ya vigezo kuu vya ukuaji na mabadiliko ya lugha ni kuongezeka kwa istilahi. Kulingana na Adolph (2019), ili istilahi ziongezeke katika lugha, ni lazima istilahi mpya ziundwe. Masharti huundwa katika lugha ili utamaduni wake uweze kukidhi dhana ambazo hapo awali hazikuwa sehemu ya utamaduni huo. Ujumbe huu ni muhimu sana katika makala haya kwani unaonyesha jinsi lugha inavyokua na kukidhi mahitaji ya mawasiliano miongoni mwa wanajamii. Makala haya yanaangazia mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo ya istilahi za Kiingereza hadi Kiswahili na athari zake kwa kuzingatia fani za biolojia, fizikia na kemia, tofauti na utafiti wa Adolph (2019), ambao unachunguza ukuzaji wa lugha ya Kiswahili kupitia utohoaji wa istilahi za kimatibabu na kompyuta. Wataalamu wengi walioshughulikia ukopaji wanakubali kwamba ukopaji ni uhamishaji wa vipengele vya kileksika kutoka lugha moja hadi nyingine (Haugen, 1950; Polomé, 1980; Adolph, 2014; Winford, 2003). Makala haya yamegawanyika katika sehemu tano: Sehemu ya kwanza ni utangulizi, ambamo dhana ya jumla ya tafsiri na kazi zake zimeelezwa, pamoja na dhana ya tafsiri ya mkopo. Sehemu ya pili inaeleza nadharia iliyoongoza uchanganuzi wa data katika makala haya. Sehemu ya tatu inaelezea mbinu. Sehemu ya nne inachambua data za mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo kutoka Kiingereza hadi Kiswahili na athari zake. Mjadala unahusu istilahi katika nyanja za biolojia, fizikia, na kemia kutoka katika Kamusi ya Biolojia, Fizikia, na Kemia (2012). Sehemu ya tano ni hitimisho. Nadharia  
Nadharia ya Istilahi za Kisayansi ilitumika kutoa data ya makala haya. Nadharia ya Istilahi za Kisayansi inahusishwa na Kiingi (1989), ambaye ndiye mwanzilishi wa nadharia hii. Baadaye, nadharia hii iliendelezwa zaidi na Kiingi (1992, 1998); Mwaro-Were (2000, 2001); Kevogo, Mukuthuria, na Ontieri (2018); na Kevogo (2020). Nadharia hii ina vigezo vya kisayansi vya istilahi bora, ambavyo vina jukumu kuu katika tathmini iliyofanywa katika makala yetu. Wataalamu kadhaa, kama vile Tumbo-Masabo na Mwansoko (2008), wameeleza kwa uwazi kanuni mbalimbali zinazopaswa kufuatwa wakati wa ukopaji, urekebishaji na uundaji wa istilahi kutoka lugha za asili na za kigeni hadi Kiswahili. Kanuni hizi zimefafanuliwa zaidi katika Tumbo-Masabo na Mwansoko (2008). Hii inahusisha kuunda istilahi kwa kutumia Kiswahili, lugha za Kibantu, lugha nyingine za Kiafrika, na lugha za kigeni. Pamoja na maoni mengine mengi yaliyotolewa na Tumbo-Masabo na Mwansoko (1997) kuhusu kanuni hizi, wanapendekeza miongozo ifuatayo: Istilahi ziakisi sifa bainifu za dhana zinazowakilisha (au angalau zipendekeze vipengele hivyo) na ziwe wazi kwa watumiaji wanaokusudiwa. Iwapo istilahi imeundwa kwa kutumia mbinu ya kuchanganya na kuchanganya maneno, vipengele vifuatavyo lazima zizingatiwe:
Idadi ya maneno yaliyounganishwa au yaliyounganishwa haipaswi kuzidi mbili. Vistawishi havipaswi kutumiwa kutenganisha istilahi ambatani, kwa sababu katika Kiswahili istilahi hizo kwa kawaida hutamkwa kama neno moja, huku mkazo wa msingi ukiwa katika silabi moja tu. Kwa mfano: -zao mtiririko ("flow products") na -nusu kipenyo ("semi-diameter"). Istilahi hizo hazipaswi kuwa na silabi zaidi ya nne, kwani maneno ya Kiswahili kwa kawaida huwa na wastani wa kati ya silabi moja hadi tano. Istilahi lazima zitolewe kwa kiwango kikubwa ili kuzalisha istilahi nyingine zinazohusiana ndani ya kikoa au sehemu husika. Hii itaruhusu istilahi zinazowakilisha dhana zinazohusiana kwa karibu au zilizounganishwa kimantiki kuonyesha muunganisho huo. Kwa mfano: taifa ("nation"), taifisha ("nationalize"), utaifa ("nationalism"), -a kitaifa ("national"), -sio na taifa ("stateless"), na -siyo wa taifa ("un-national"). Istilahi (hasa zile zilizo na vivuli vya maana vinavyopishana) lazima zidumishe uthabiti katika mfuatano. Maneno yafuatayo, kwa mfano, yanaonyesha upatanisho unaokubalika wa mfuatano: tabakanje, tabakandani, tabakamzunguko, tabakakati, na kadhalika. Istilahi lazima iwe ya kutosha, ikimaanisha inapaswa kuonyesha sifa za dhana wanazowakilisha (na sio, kwa mfano, kuzipinga). Kwa mfano, neno “tahakiki ya maandishi” halifai kwa sababu kwa ujumla hurejelea tathmini ya uandishi kwa jumla, badala ya uchanganuzi au uhakiki wa fasihi. Istilahi lazima pia ziwe fupi na zinazoeleweka. Maneno marefu, kama vile “majira ya majani kupukutika” (msimu wa kiangazi unapokaribia), hayafai kwa sababu hayazingatii kanuni ya uchumi wa lugha. Kanuni hizi ni muhimu katika uundaji wa istilahi kwani hutoa mwongozo juu ya kile kinachofaa kufanywa kuhusu kukopa, kuunda, na kurekebisha. Aidha, mbinu za kuunda istilahi zimependekezwa. Hebu tuangalie njia hizi hapa chini: kwanza, tafsiri, hasa kutoka kwa lugha zinazojulikana kuwa za kimataifa, kama vile Kiingereza, Kifaransa, Kihispania, na kadhalika. Pili, kuunda istilahi kwa kuzingatia mifumo ya dhana. Nadharia hii inafaa kwani inatoa misingi ya kufuata wakati wa mchakato wa tafsiri. Kadhalika, inafafanua mbinu za uundaji istilahi. 

Mbinu  
Kila mtafiti anatumia mbinu zinazofaa na zilizo wazi kwa ajili ya utafiti wao. Makala haya ni matokeo ya utafiti wa kimaelezo uliofanywa maktabani na nyanjani. Mtafiti alikusanya data kutoka Idara ya Lugha za Kigeni na Isimu, TATAKI kutoka Chuo Kikuu cha Dar es Salaam, pamoja na BAKIZA Wilaya ya Ubungo, Mkoa wa Dar es Salaam, ambapo data zilikusanywa kwa kutumia mahojiano, hojaji, na chanzo cha data za maktaba. Kwa mujibu wa Krishnaswami na Ranganatham (2005), mahojiano ni mbinu ya kukusanya data ambayo huhusisha mabadilishano kati ya mtafiti na mhojiwa kwa lengo la kupata taarifa zinazohusiana na mada inayochunguzwa. Kwa kutumia mbinu ya usaili, mtafiti aliweza kufanya mahojiano ya ana kwa ana na wataalamu wa tafsiri kutoka idara na taasisi zilizotajwa hapo juu. Hojaji huandaliwa kwa lengo la kukusanya taarifa muhimu kutoka kwa wahojiwa (Mugenda na Mugenda, 2003). Mbinu ya dodoso inaweza kufanywa ana kwa ana au kwa njia zisizo za ana kwa ana, kulingana na maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia. Maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia yamewezesha utumaji wa dodoso mbalimbali na watafiti kwa wahojiwa wao kwa njia ya kielektroniki (kupitia mtandao na barua pepe). Hata hivyo, mtafiti wa makala haya alitumia hojaji za ana kwa ana kwa sababu watoa taarifa walikuwa katika eneo moja na kufikika kwa urahisi. Aidha, mtafiti alipitia maandishi mbalimbali kama vile majarida, tasnifu, kamusi na kadhalika kutoka katika chanzo cha data za maktaba. Matokeo ya Utafiti

Matokeo ya makala haya yalipatikana baada ya uchunguzi na uchambuzi wa data zinazohusu ukuzaji wa Kiswahili kupitia tafsiri ya mkopo ya istilahi kutoka Kiingereza. Tafsiri ya mkopo ni mkakati wa kuunda neno linalohusisha uhamishaji wa neno kwa neno wa vipengele vya kimuundo na dhana za jumla. Muundo wa istilahi unaoundwa kwa kutumia mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo hubadilika ili kuendana na kanuni za kimofolojia na kifonolojia za lugha lengwa. Kutokana na mbinu za usaili, hojaji, na chanzo cha data za maktaba, ilibainika kuwa istilahi kadhaa katika nyanja za biolojia, fizikia, na kemia—kupitia Kamusi ya Biolojia, Fizikia na Kemia (2012)—zimejumuishwa katika Kiswahili kutoka Kiingereza kupitia mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo. The findings of this article indicate that terminology in biology, chemistry, and physics has been translated through the strategy of loan translation from English into Swahili. Hii inatokana na mahitaji makubwa ya istilahi hizi miongoni mwa watumiaji wa Kiswahili, pamoja na maendeleo na ukuaji wa sayansi na teknolojia. Hali hii inawalazimu Waswahili kutumia mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo ili kukidhi mahitaji ya mawasiliano ya wazungumzaji wa Kiswahili na kujumuisha dhana zinazotokana na istilahi hizi. Manufaa kwa Watafsiri wa Lugha na Utambuzi wa Kimataifa wa TUKI

Mkakati wa kukopa istilahi za Kiingereza kwa Kiswahili kupitia tafsiri ya mkopo kama mbinu ya kuunda istilahi za Kiswahili umekuwa na mchango mkubwa katika kutoa fursa kwa wafasiri wa lugha. Kwa mfano, TUKI (2012) imetafsiri msamiati wa kutosha unaohusiana na fani za biolojia, fizikia na kemia kwa kutumia mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo na aina nyinginezo za ukopaji; hata hivyo, makala haya yanaangazia mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo. Taasisi hii imetafsiri msamiati kutoka kwa biolojia, fizikia, na kemia kutoka Kiingereza hadi Kiswahili. Hakika kazi hii imeiletea TUKI sifa duniani kutokana na umuhimu wake mkubwa katika nyanja za biolojia, fizikia na kemia. Kando na kutambuliwa kimataifa, wale wanaohusika katika kazi hii pia wamenufaika kiuchumi kutokana na mauzo yanayofanywa kupitia vitabu vilivyochapishwa, vikiwemo Biolojia, Fizikia na Kamusi ya Kemia sanifu. Hii inachangiwa na umuhimu wa yaliyomo, uangalifu unaochukuliwa katika utayarishaji wake, na hasa utaalamu na taaluma ya watunzi wa kamusi. Hii inaonyesha wazi kwamba watumiaji wake wana imani kubwa na kamusi hii na kwa hivyo wako tayari kufanya manunuzi bila kusita. Kuenea Ulimwenguni kwa Lugha ya Kiswahili

Kulingana na taarifa kutoka kwa watafitiwa (data ya shambani) pamoja na data za maktaba, mtafiti amegundua kuwa mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo uliotekelezwa na TUKI (2012) umechangia kutambulika kwa Kiswahili duniani kote, kwa kuwa fani za biolojia, fizikia na kemia zinatumika duniani kutokana na maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia, pamoja na umuhimu wake kwa wanafunzi wanaosoma masomo haya na kwa wazungumzaji wa lugha ya Kiswahili kwa ujumla. Zaidi ya hayo, wazungumzaji wa lugha nyingine mbali na Kiswahili wanahitaji kujifunza msamiati wa nyanja hizi katika lugha ya Kiswahili. Hali hii inawapelekea kupata vitabu kadhaa vya lugha ya Kiswahili, ikiwemo kamusi hii. Mambo haya yote yamechangia pakubwa kuenea kwa Kiswahili kote ulimwenguni. Kuenea kwa Kiswahili ulimwenguni kote kumewatia moyo watu kutoka nchi mbalimbali kujifunza Kiswahili, kukithamini, na kukithamini sana.

Hitimisho

Uchambuzi katika makala haya unathibitisha hoja kwamba mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo umetumika kuwa mojawapo ya mbinu za kuazima istilahi za Kiingereza kwa Kiswahili. Maneno yaliyochunguzwa katika makala haya ni yale ya nyanja za biolojia, fizikia, na kemia. Kwa upande wa biolojia, maneno kama vile: abductor, abiotic, mizizi ya angani, basal bone, mimea ya kila miaka miwili, nitrojeni, oksiputi, spermatid, na zoology ilitambuliwa. Mtafiti pia alizingatia mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo katika uwanja wa kemia. Yafuatayo ni baadhi ya masharti yanayoshughulikiwa katika nyanja hii: kamili, asetati, wingi amilifu, masi tendaji, acylation, nishati ya dhamana, dawa ya kuulia wadudu, mionzi ya x na uzimolojia. Introduction  
Translation is the act of transferring a message contained in writing from the source language to the target language without altering the intended meaning in the source language. Thus, translation is regarded as a method of learning foreign languages, showcasing various cultures, and transmitting the knowledge and skills of other communities, such as information on scientific and technological advancements. The motivation that drives a person to translate the message from the source language to the target language is the desire to facilitate communication among speakers of different languages. We can therefore say that translation is a means or even a bridge to bring together various communities that speak different languages. Moreover, loan translation is one method of coining new vocabulary, where a concept from the source language is adopted and translated into the target language; for example, Army worm – kiwavi jeshi, tap root – mzizi pau, and so on. The strategy of borrowing through loan translation has gained momentum due to the significant developments occurring in the field of science and technology, coupled with society’s advancement into modernity, resulting in a high demand for vocabulary to describe various concepts. The researcher of this article investigates the loan translation strategy of English vocabulary into Kiswahili.

Utangulizi  
Tafsiri ni kitendo cha kuhamisha ujumbe ulio katika maandishi kutoka lugha chanzi hadi lugha lengwa bila kubadilisha maana iliyokusudiwa katika lugha chanzi. Kwa hivyo, tafsiri inachukuliwa kuwa njia ya kujifunza lugha za kigeni, kuonyesha tamaduni mbalimbali, na kusambaza ujuzi na ujuzi wa jamii nyingine, kama vile habari juu ya maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia. Motisha inayomsukuma mtu kutafsiri ujumbe kutoka lugha chanzi hadi lugha lengwa ni hamu ya kurahisisha mawasiliano miongoni mwa wazungumzaji wa lugha mbalimbali. Kwa hiyo tunaweza kusema kuwa tafsiri ni njia au hata daraja la kuzikutanisha jamii mbalimbali zinazozungumza lugha mbalimbali. Aidha, tafsiri ya mkopo ni mbinu mojawapo ya kubuni msamiati mpya, ambapo dhana kutoka katika lugha chanzi hupitishwa na kutafsiriwa katika lugha lengwa; kwa mfano, Army worm – kiwavi jeshi, tap root – mzizi pau, na kadhalika. Mkakati wa kukopa kupitia tafsiri ya mkopo umeshika kasi kutokana na maendeleo makubwa yanayotokea katika nyanja ya sayansi na teknolojia, pamoja na maendeleo ya jamii katika usasa, na kusababisha uhitaji mkubwa wa msamiati wa kuelezea dhana mbalimbali. Mtafiti wa makala haya anachunguza mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo wa msamiati wa Kiingereza hadi Kiswahili.

discourses.source_txt: Several scholars, such as Tumbo-Masabo and Mwansoko (2008), have clearly outlined various principles that should be followed during the borrowing, adaptation, and formation of terminology from indigenous and foreign languages into Swahili. These principles are elaborated in Tumbo-Masabo and Mwansoko (2008).
discourses.translated_txt: Wataalamu kadhaa, kama vile Tumbo-Masabo na Mwansoko (2008), wameeleza kwa uwazi kanuni mbalimbali zinazopaswa kufuatwa wakati wa ukopaji, urekebishaji na uundaji wa istilahi kutoka lugha za asili na za kigeni hadi Kiswahili. Kanuni hizi zimefafanuliwa zaidi katika Tumbo-Masabo na Mwansoko (2008).

discourses.source_txt:
This involves creating terminology using Swahili, Bantu languages, other African languages, and foreign languages. In addition to many other views expressed by Tumbo-Masabo and Mwansoko (1997) regarding these principles, they recommend the following guidelines: Terminology should reflect the distinctive features of the concepts they represent (or at least suggest such features) and be clear to the intended users. If terminology is formed using compounding and word combination techniques, the following aspects must be considered:
The number of words combined or joined should not exceed two. Hyphens should not be used to separate compound terms, because in Swahili such terms are usually pronounced as a single word, with the primary stress on only one syllable. For example: -zao mtiririko ("flow products") and -nusu kipenyo ("semi-diameter"). Such terms should not have more than four syllables, since Swahili words usually have an average of between one and five syllables. Terminology must be highly derivable in order to generate other related terms within the relevant domain or field. This will allow terms representing closely related or derivationally connected concepts to logically reflect that connection. For example: taifa ("nation"), taifisha ("nationalize"), utaifa ("nationalism"), -a kitaifa ("national"), -sio na taifa ("stateless"), and -siyo wa taifa ("un-national").
discourses.translated_txt:
Hii inahusisha kuunda istilahi kwa kutumia Kiswahili, lugha za Kibantu, lugha nyingine za Kiafrika, na lugha za kigeni. Pamoja na maoni mengine mengi yaliyotolewa na Tumbo-Masabo na Mwansoko (1997) kuhusu kanuni hizi, wanapendekeza miongozo ifuatayo: Istilahi ziakisi sifa bainifu za dhana zinazowakilisha (au angalau zipendekeze vipengele hivyo) na ziwe wazi kwa watumiaji wanaokusudiwa. Iwapo istilahi imeundwa kwa kutumia mbinu ya kuchanganya na kuchanganya maneno, vipengele vifuatavyo lazima zizingatiwe:
Idadi ya maneno yaliyounganishwa au yaliyounganishwa haipaswi kuzidi mbili. Vistawishi havipaswi kutumiwa kutenganisha istilahi ambatani, kwa sababu katika Kiswahili istilahi hizo kwa kawaida hutamkwa kama neno moja, huku mkazo wa msingi ukiwa katika silabi moja tu. Kwa mfano: -zao mtiririko ("flow products") na -nusu kipenyo ("semi-diameter"). Istilahi hizo hazipaswi kuwa na silabi zaidi ya nne, kwani maneno ya Kiswahili kwa kawaida huwa na wastani wa kati ya silabi moja hadi tano. Istilahi lazima zitolewe kwa kiwango kikubwa ili kuzalisha istilahi nyingine zinazohusiana ndani ya kikoa au sehemu husika. Hii itaruhusu istilahi zinazowakilisha dhana zinazohusiana kwa karibu au zilizounganishwa kimantiki kuonyesha muunganisho huo. Kwa mfano: taifa ("nation"), taifisha ("nationalize"), utaifa ("nationalism"), -a kitaifa ("national"), -sio na taifa ("stateless"), na -siyo wa taifa ("un-national").

discourses.source_txt: Terminology (especially those with overlapping shades of meaning) must maintain consistency in sequence. The following terms, for example, demonstrate an acceptable alignment of sequence: tabakanje, tabakandani, tabakamzunguko, tabakakati, and so on. Terminology must be adequate, meaning it should reflect the characteristics of the concepts they represent (and not, for instance, contradict them). For example, the term “tahakiki ya maandishi” is inappropriate because it generally refers to the evaluation of writing at large, rather than the analysis or critique of literature. Terminology must also be short and understandable. Lengthy terms, such as “majira ya majani kupukutika” (when the dry season approaches), are unsuitable because they do not adhere to the principle of linguistic economy.

discourses.source_txt:
Research Findings

The findings of this article were obtained after an investigation and analysis of data concerning the development of Swahili through the loan translation of terminology from English. Loan translation is a strategy for term creation involving word-for-word transfer of both structural elements and general concepts. The structure of terms created using the loan translation strategy changes to conform to the morphological and phonological rules of the target language. From the methods of interviews, questionnaires, and the library data source, it was found that several terms in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry—through the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary (2012)—have been incorporated into Swahili from English via the loan translation strategy.

The Loan Translation Strategy of English Terms into Swahili and Its Effects: An Analysis of Selected Entries from the Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary

Benefits for Language Translators and Global Recognition of TUKI

The strategy of borrowing English terms into Swahili through loan translation as a method for creating Swahili terminology has played a significant role in providing opportunities for language translators. For instance, TUKI (2012) has translated an adequate vocabulary related to the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry by employing the loan translation strategy and other forms of borrowing; however, this article focuses on the loan translation strategy. This institution has translated vocabulary from biology, physics, and chemistry from English into Swahili. Indeed, this work has brought global recognition to TUKI due to its great importance in the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry. Alongside international recognition, those involved in this work have also benefited economically from sales made through published books, including the standardized Biology, Physics, and Chemistry Dictionary. This is attributed to the significance of its contents, the care taken in its preparation, and especially the expertise and professionalism of the dictionary’s compilers.

Manufaa kwa Watafsiri wa Lugha na Utambuzi wa Kimataifa wa TUKI

Mkakati wa kukopa istilahi za Kiingereza kwa Kiswahili kupitia tafsiri ya mkopo kama mbinu ya kuunda istilahi za Kiswahili umekuwa na mchango mkubwa katika kutoa fursa kwa wafasiri wa lugha. Kwa mfano, TUKI (2012) imetafsiri msamiati wa kutosha unaohusiana na fani za biolojia, fizikia na kemia kwa kutumia mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo na aina nyinginezo za ukopaji; hata hivyo, makala haya yanaangazia mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo. Taasisi hii imetafsiri msamiati kutoka kwa biolojia, fizikia, na kemia kutoka Kiingereza hadi Kiswahili. Hakika kazi hii imeiletea TUKI sifa duniani kutokana na umuhimu wake mkubwa katika nyanja za biolojia, fizikia na kemia. Kando na kutambuliwa kimataifa, wale wanaohusika katika kazi hii pia wamenufaika kiuchumi kutokana na mauzo yanayofanywa kupitia vitabu vilivyochapishwa, vikiwemo Biolojia, Fizikia na Kamusi ya Kemia sanifu. Hii inachangiwa na umuhimu wa yaliyomo, uangalifu unaochukuliwa katika utayarishaji wake, na hasa utaalamu na taaluma ya watunzi wa kamusi.

The Global Spread of the Swahili Language

Based on information from respondents (field data) as well as library data, the researcher has found that the loan translation strategy implemented by TUKI (2012) has contributed to the worldwide recognition of Swahili, since the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry are used globally due to advancements in science and technology, as well as their importance to students studying these subjects and to Swahili speakers in general. Furthermore, speakers of other languages apart from Swahili need to learn the vocabulary of these fields in the Swahili language. This situation leads them to acquire several Swahili language books, including this dictionary. All these factors have significantly contributed to the overall spread of Swahili throughout the world. The global spread of Swahili has encouraged people from various countries to learn Swahili, appreciate it, and value it highly.

Conclusion

The analysis in this article confirms the argument that the loan translation strategy has been used as one of the methods for borrowing English terminology into Swahili. The terms examined in this article are those from the fields of biology, physics, and chemistry. In the case of biology, terms such as: abductor, abiotic, aerial roots, basal bone, biennial plants, nitrogen, occiput, spermatid, and zoology were identified. The researcher also considered the loan translation strategy in the field of chemistry.

Kuenea Ulimwenguni kwa Lugha ya Kiswahili

Kulingana na taarifa kutoka kwa watafitiwa (data ya shambani) pamoja na data za maktaba, mtafiti amegundua kuwa mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo uliotekelezwa na TUKI (2012) umechangia kutambulika kwa Kiswahili duniani kote, kwa kuwa fani za biolojia, fizikia na kemia zinatumika duniani kutokana na maendeleo ya sayansi na teknolojia, pamoja na umuhimu wake kwa wanafunzi wanaosoma masomo haya na kwa wazungumzaji wa lugha ya Kiswahili kwa ujumla. Zaidi ya hayo, wazungumzaji wa lugha nyingine mbali na Kiswahili wanahitaji kujifunza msamiati wa nyanja hizi katika lugha ya Kiswahili. Hali hii inawapelekea kupata vitabu kadhaa vya lugha ya Kiswahili, ikiwemo kamusi hii. Mambo haya yote yamechangia pakubwa kuenea kwa Kiswahili kote ulimwenguni. Kuenea kwa Kiswahili ulimwenguni kote kumewatia moyo watu kutoka nchi mbalimbali kujifunza Kiswahili, kukithamini, na kukithamini sana.

Hitimisho

Uchambuzi katika makala haya unathibitisha hoja kwamba mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo umetumika kuwa mojawapo ya mbinu za kuazima istilahi za Kiingereza kwa Kiswahili. Maneno yaliyochunguzwa katika makala haya ni yale ya nyanja za biolojia, fizikia, na kemia. Kwa upande wa biolojia, maneno kama vile: abductor, abiotic, mizizi ya angani, basal bone, mimea ya kila miaka miwili, nitrojeni, oksiputi, spermatid, na zoology ilitambuliwa. Mtafiti pia alizingatia mkakati wa tafsiri ya mkopo katika uwanja wa kemia.
